transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Rachel Kim (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood CSM), Evan Ortiz (Verdant VP Eng), Maya Chen (Verdant SRE), Liam Patel (Verdant Security), Jules Rivera (Verdant Product)

Auto-summary: Follow-up on June 11th incident where Verdant saw spikes in tail latency and some 5xxs for a small percentage of traffic during nightly ETL. Walked through mitigation plan and tests to validate fixes; discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and security questions for pilot.

00:00 Rachel: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the Verdant postmortem follow-up, um we wanted to go over the root cause analysis that Marco pulled together and map out next steps
00:12 Evan: yeah thanks Rachel, appreciate it. um we were hit pretty hard on 6/11 during our ETL job when all the enrichment calls kicked off, we saw tail latency up to 2.1s and about 0.8% 5xxs, which is outsized for us
00:30 Marco: right so we dug in, there's a couple things that lined up — first is the KV cache got effectively cold for a subset of keys because the ETL traffic touched many unique prefixes; that caused a big burst of model context loads and some bigger-than-expected decoding cost on the GPU side
00:48 Maya: totally, and from our side we saw autoscaler ramping, but the pod spin-up lag plus the initial batch sizes didn't line up with the incoming burst so a small window of requests saw degraded perf
00:59 Marco: exactly, and there were a few requests that ended up hitting the fallback model variant which has a slightly different tokenization, so the retry path added extra latency for some requests
01:12 Liam: quick Q — is the fallback path logging enough info for us to correlate request IDs? in the ticket we had trouble mapping traces to the firehose logs
01:20 Marco: short answer: not consistently, that's on us — some of the auto-logging during the fallback didn't have the request_id field populated because of a serialization bug. we've patched that in the staging branch and plan to push to prod once tests pass
01:33 Jules: hmm okay, so what's the recommended immediate mitigation while that patch lands? we need something for the next ETL run on Friday
01:40 Priya: we recommended three parallel mitigations: 1) pre-warm the KV cache for the top N prefixes based on last 7 days, 2) apply a conservative client-side rate limiter for the ETL job to smooth the burst, and 3) if you want a stronger guarantee, pilot a small Dedicated pool for the ETL window so capacity is isolated
02:05 Evan: can you explain the Dedicated option costs and what the expected latency improvement looks like?
02:12 Rachel: yeah so Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and you can pin a model variant; that removes the autoscaler cold-start risk. for latency, we generally see median improve a little but the tail is where you win — in our internal benchmarks we brought tail P95 down by 30-50% for bursty workloads when set up correctly
02:29 Maya: okay that sounds good, but we have security concerns — will any logs or data go outside our VPC? we need to pass this to our compliance folks
02:38 Rachel: for a Dedicated pilot on Redwood Dedicated we can do it in your VPC with private networking; logs and telemetry can be configured to forward to your SIEM via secure endpoints and KMS can be customer-managed. we'll include the SOC2 / ISO artifacts with the quote
02:53 Liam: thanks, please include SAML SSO config and audit log retention options — we have a 365-day retention ask for this team
03:00 Marco: noted. on the technical side, the KV cache warmup script we suggested is low-risk — it just issues synthetic prefix requests to populate the prefix cache. we'll share a script and a runbook that you can run in your staging environment before Friday's ETL
03:18 Maya: are there any concerns about cache warmup causing additional load? we don't want warmup to be just another spike
03:24 Marco: good point — the script has a pacing parameter and we recommend a two-phase warmup: slow ramp over 10 minutes then a brief higher-rate phase to reach steady state. we'll provide recommended values based on your QPS numbers
03:40 Evan: on the tracing side, once you patch the request_id serialization, can you re-run the logs from 6/11 and produce a matched timeline for us? that will help our SREs validate root cause
03:51 Marco: yes, we intend to reprocess the archived traces and backfill request ids where possible; we'll send you a CSV of matched spans and highlight the ones that hit fallback variants
04:05 Jules: one other thing — we noticed a couple of model regressions in the responses after the incident, likely from an albedo of model switching; is that expected?
04:15 Marco: that can happen if a request falls back to the smaller variant; output differences are expected. as a guardrail we recommend locking to a model hash for production-critical endpoints; Dedicated makes that straightforward
04:29 Priya: also, we're going to add an entry to the runbook for "ETL burst mode" with clear pre-checks, acceptance criteria, and rollback steps. we can share the doc and ask Verdant to review and sign off
04:43 Maya: awesome — timeline wise, we want the patch and KV warmup in staging asap and then a decision on Friday's run. can we aim to have the patch in staging by Tuesday?
04:53 Marco: yes, patch in staging by Tuesday EOD is doable; warmup script and parameters we'll upload today to the shared folder
05:02 Rachel: quick recap then — Marco will push patch and share tests, Verdant to provide log samples, Rachel will send Dedicated quote, Priya will circulate runbook. we'll reconvene after the next ETL run or earlier if issues remain
05:16 Evan: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround
05:20 Rachel: thanks folks, we'll follow up in email with links. bye

Notes and references: "KV cache warmup script" (link: //drive.redwood/kvcache-warmup.sh), "Dedicated pilot terms" (link: //drive.redwood/dedicated-pilot-verdant.pdf), "Patch PR #482" (link: //github.redwood/pr/482).

End of transcript.
